title: Why Every Student Needs A Whiteboard
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that personal whiteboards are one of the most underrated classroom tools, but only when their use is narrowly restricted to a single purpose: checking for understanding immediately before releasing students to independent work. He warns explicitly against letting students use whiteboards for open-ended brainstorming or drawing, since unrestricted use causes more problems than it solves. His central claim is that checking for understanding is the critical gate before independence, and whiteboards let a teacher verify every student's grasp of a concept in seconds, see exactly who does and doesn't understand, and get instant feedback on the lesson's own effectiveness. The concrete technique is to make whiteboard checks the final step before the 'Go' signal, posing a question whose answer -- a drawing, word, solution, or graph -- can be shown on a small board, then reteaching on the spot if responses reveal confusion.
points: Whiteboards should be used for exactly one purpose -- checking for understanding -- never for open-ended brainstorming or drawing.
A whiteboard check lets a teacher see every student's understanding in seconds and get instant feedback on the lesson's own clarity.
Whiteboard checks work best as the final step immediately before giving the 'Go' signal to begin independent work.
Using whiteboards regularly makes a teacher a better lesson-deliverer over time because the feedback is undeniable and immediate.
quotes: Every student in your class needs their own personal whiteboard. They need to know where to keep it, how to care for it, and when to use it.
Whiteboards should never be used independently. Allowing students to pull them out to brainstorm ideas, work out math problems, or draw superheros causes more problems than they’re worth.
Checking for understanding is critical for the transition to independent work. Whiteboards enable you to send students off knowing they can do the work without any help.
They’re best used as the final step before giving your “Go” signal to begin independent work.
If your lesson was less than clear, their responses will show you where and how you need to reteach or clarify.
One other benefit is that because whiteboards provide you with undeniable feedback, you become very good at delivering lessons.
